turns.t: Good afternoon, doctor. I do apologise for troubling you, but my voice has gone. It's been a little over a week now.
Good afternoon. Not at all. Let me hear you. Can you say your name and where you live? ~
Margaret Ashworth, number twelve, Birch Road. You can see it's quite croaky. ~
I can hear it, a bit husky. When did it come on, exactly?
Ten days ago, rather suddenly. I woke up and it simply wasn't there, I could only whisper.
Had you been ill, a cold or a cough, beforehand? ~
Nothing at all. I'd been to my choir the night before, mind you, and we did the whole of the Messiah. ~
Ah. Enthusiastic singing could do that. And how has it been since? Is it improving or staying the same? ~
A little better in the mornings, but by the evening it's worse again. ~
Do you have any pain in your throat, or difficulty swallowing? ~
No pain to speak of, and I can swallow perfectly well. It's just the voice. ~
Right. You're not on any regular treatment I should know about? ~
No, I'm very fortunate. I take nothing at all, except a vitamin on Sundays. ~
Good. Any other health conditions?
I have a touch of acid reflux, nothing major.
That's useful. Open wide and say ahh for me. ~
Ahh.
Throat looks fine. The vocal cords are inside, so I can't see them from here. ~
Quite so. What do you think it is? ~
A sudden husky voice after heavy use, with some reflux in the background, looks most like laryngitis.
Laryngitis. Is that serious? ~
Not usually. The cords are inflamed, like a sprained ankle, and they need to rest. ~
I see. Then I shall be silent on the subject of Handel. ~
Exactly, no singing, and avoid whispering too, which strains the cords just as much.
Whispering is bad? ~
Yes, a gentle, easy speaking voice is better. Drink plenty of water, and avoid shouting or clearing your throat. ~
I do clear my throat a great deal. ~
Try sipping water instead. ~
How long until it improves? ~
Often a couple of weeks. If it's not back to normal in three weeks, I'd like you seen by a specialist who can look at the cords directly.
Three weeks, understood. Thank you, doctor. ~
Rest that voice. ~

follow_up.time_reference: if it's not back to normal in three weeks
